R6I-bear-backcountry-0003.name: 130 m NW of Trapline Creek
R6I-bear-backcountry-0003.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R6I-bear-backcountry-0003.parkWhat: pull off on Clore M/L Br 636000 (gravel road)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2012 (14 years old), 130 m SE: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
S facing slope, 14 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Trapline Creek 130 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from City of Terrace, about 46 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Beam Station Rd, Queensway Dr, Hwy 16 and 37, Copper River FSR.
Park: 54.42176, -128.04058, pull off on Clore M/L Br 636000 (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: 5.2 km SW, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 370 m, about 142 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 140 m SE of the spot at 541 m (54.40225, -128.11338). Water: Trapline Creek right here (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 6-9, Region 6. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-01, closures 2026-10-16.

R6I-grouse-atv-0001.name: 190 m SE of Trapline Creek
R6I-grouse-atv-0001.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).

evidence.t: 100% of the stretch in grouse forest zones (BWBS, CWH, ESSF, ICH, IDF, MS, SBPS, SBS).
6 cutblocks touch the road (30 years old or less): edges and clover.
9 wetlands, lakes or creeks along the road: riparian edges.
Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).
